```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.path = "figures/",
  out.width = "100%",
  collapse_output = TRUE
)

# Hook to wrap output in collapsible details
knitr::knit_hooks$set(
  output = function(x, options) {
    if (!is.null(options$collapse_output)) {
      summary_text <- if (is.character(options$collapse_output)) {
        options$collapse_output
      } else {
        "Click to see output"
      }
      paste0(
        "<details><summary>", summary_text, "</summary>\n\n",
        "```\n", x, "```\n",
        "</details>\n"
      )
    } else {
      paste0("```\n", x, "```\n")
    }
  },
  message = function(x, options) {
    if (!is.null(options$collapse_output)) {
      summary_text <- if (is.character(options$collapse_output)) {
        options$collapse_output
      } else {
        "Click to see messages"
      }
      paste0(
        "<details><summary>", summary_text, "</summary>\n\n",
        "```\n", x, "```\n",
        "</details>\n"
      )
    } else {
      paste0("```\n", x, "```\n")
    }
  },
  warning = function(x, options) {
    if (!is.null(options$collapse_output)) {
      summary_text <- if (is.character(options$collapse_output)) {
        options$collapse_output
      } else {
        "Click to see warnings"
      }
      paste0(
        "<details><summary>", summary_text, "</summary>\n\n",
        "```\n", x, "```\n",
        "</details>\n"
      )
    } else {
      paste0("```\n", x, "```\n")
    }
  }
)
```

/!\ Work in progress /!\

In this vignette we will explore the notion of "Bayesian surprise" applied to the 
presence of a given taxa in our sample(s). The idea is to quantify how surprising,
(the ratio between prior and posterior probabilities) it is to find a given taxa
in a given location.
